{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA), so selection turns on strength and comparability of evidence. PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused, large multi-cohort AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) with European evaluation, which domain guidance prioritizes over pan-trait/portability framework scores when endpoint alignment is similar. Competing models have notable limitations: PGS001784 (Cell Genom) is explicitly a global biobank framework score and its reported AUROC=0.868 is a full-model metric with heavy covariates, while the PRS-only R2 is small (0.014661), so the high AUROC is likely covariate-driven and not directly comparable; PGS002054 is a UKB portability framework score with only partial-r=0.0144; PGS003429 has only full-model AUROC=0.708 with unknown covariates and is framed around cost-effectiveness/screening; PGS000753 is disease-focused but very sparse (29 variants) and reports only an OR per SD (1.37) without AUC/R2. Remaining limitation: for PGS003972 the available performance evidence is only a full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates and no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, making cross-model performance comparison uncertain; therefore confidence is moderate and the outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (or near-equivalent) and European evaluation available. Competing candidates either come from portability/framework contexts (PGS002054 ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores…’ with only partial-r; PGS001784 ‘Global Biobank analyses…’ with full-model AUROC likely covariate-influenced despite reporting PGS-only R2), or have performance reported only as full-model discrimination with unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972) or a high C-index without PRS-only metrics (PGS003973). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-aligned phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is explicitly prevalent). Among them, PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with a clear per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which provides PRS-specific signal without relying on potentially covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with diagnosis-like endpoints (no explicit proxy/horizon mismatch), but their performance evidence is not cleanly comparable: several report only full-model discrimination (e.g., PGS001784 AUROC=0.868 with heavy covariates; PGS003973 C-index=0.882 with age/sex), while others lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and/or covariates are unknown (PGS003429/PGS003972). PGS000753 comes from a disease-focused AAA publication (Million Veteran Program architecture study), uses a clear prevalent AAA endpoint with light covariates (age, sex, PCs), and provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) plus moderate external validation size (n=46,564) in Europeans, avoiding over-reliance on potentially covariate-driven full-model AUROC. Limitation: it is a sparse P+T score (29 variants) and lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, while some competitors provide PRS-only R2/partial-r; however those competitors are framework/portability-style or have unclear covariate comparability, so the best-supported choice remains PGS000753 but with only moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and use a direct disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported is AAA for all), so selection hinges on comparability of PRS-specific performance evidence, covariate burden/clarity, validation support, and study archetype. PGS003972 (Nat Genet 2023 GWAS meta-analysis) is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused, multi-cohort AAA meta-analysis with broad external cohort involvement (many listed cohorts) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), which together provide stronger endpoint-focused development/transportability evidence than the two clear framework-style scores (PGS001784: ‘Global Biobank analyses…’ and PGS002054: ‘Portability of 245 polygenic scores…’). Among the Nat Genet pair, PGS003973 reports a very high full-model C-index (0.882) with only age/age^2/sex covariates, but this is not explicitly PGS-only; given domain guidance not to substitute full-model discrimination for PRS-only performance, that metric is less directly comparable for ranking. PGS003972 reports a more typical full-model AUROC (0.69) but has more than one validation record (record_count=3), suggesting somewhat broader reported performance evidence than PGS003973 (record_count=1). Remaining limitation: across candidates, PRS-only AUROC is generally missing and several reported discriminations are full-model/ambiguous (and covariates are unknown for PGS003429/PGS003972), so the evidence does not support a clearly high-confidence winner despite the stronger disease-focused study context for PGS003972."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection turns on endpoint fidelity (similar across models), PRS-comparable performance evidence, covariate comparability, and study archetype. PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA paper (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) and reports a meaningful PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with relatively basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–5) and a moderate validation size (n=46,564), which together provide a coherent, endpoint-faithful evidence package. Competing models either come from framework/portability-style efforts with metrics that are not clearly PRS-only (PGS001784 full-model AUROC 0.868 with extensive covariates; PGS002054 from a UKB portability paper with only partial-r 0.0144), or report only full-model discrimination without clear PRS-only contribution and/or unknown covariates (PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973). PGS003973 reports a high C-index (0.882) but with no PRS-only metric and limited validation size (~7,517) plus ambiguity about how much is covariate-driven, so it is not enough to clearly outrank the disease-focused MVP model. Overall, the choice is sub-optimal because PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics are largely missing or non-comparable across candidates, leaving residual uncertainty in cross-model ranking."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (mostly simply “abdominal aortic aneurysm”; PGS000753 is “prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm”), so selection turns on comparably interpretable PRS performance and study archetype. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_efo = age-related macular degeneration), but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity, study archetype, and metric interpretability.
